No Fixed Address

In the passing game the ball funnels to Justin Jefferson — 30% of targets (league ~23%), a genuine alpha share that concentrates the receiving value at the top.

The Offensive Blueprint

MIN throw by design. They pass +1% over expectation (league -2%) and keep firing even with a lead (42% early-down pass when ahead vs ~41%) — the kind of pass-first identity that keeps receivers live in every script.

They're a heavy under-center team (54% shotgun vs ~68%) — a pro-style, run-committed structure.

The WR2 is unusually involved here — 18% of targets (league ~15%), meaning there's bankable volume beyond the top receiver.

When they fall behind they abandon the run entirely — 59% pass while trailing, so their pass-catchers have huge comeback-script ceilings.

This is a deliberate, low-volume offense — just 58 plays a game (league ~61), which quietly caps the ceiling on everybody's targets and carries.

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they stay aggressive, throwing 61% of the time, which puts scoring equity on Justin Jefferson.

Defense — A Balanced Defense

Soft against opposing WR2s — 53 rec yds/game (vs ~36). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 109 rushing and 220 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

They lock down backs out of the backfield — just 12 rec yds/game (vs ~18); fade receiving props there.

A stingy, efficient defense — just 41% success allowed (vs ~44%); temper expectations for opposing skill players.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: their pass-catchers have massive ceilings in comeback scripts (fade-material as underdogs).

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
